sources_considered.why: Contemporary survey directly connects opacity with debugging difficulty and describes explanation-based debugging research.
The February 2022 version documents mechanism tracing and targeted weight editing before the post.
Read the training-process discussion. It documents practical difficulties and adjustments, but does not isolate opacity as their cause; hardware problems are also prominent.

evidence_items.publisher: arXiv; Piyawat Lertvittayakumjorn and Francesca Toni
evidence_items.explanation: The survey supports the narrower causal point that opacity makes locating and repairing problems harder. Its review of explanation-based debugging also shows that researchers were already developing remedies.

evidence_items.publisher: arXiv; Kevin Meng, David Bau, Alex Andonian and Yonatan Belinkov

receipt.public_excerpt: editing facts stored in model weights.

evidence_items.explanation: The authors used causal interventions to investigate factual recall and evaluated targeted factual edits on CounterFact. This supplies a concrete pre-post example of useful mechanistic understanding and repair without adding data or layers.

unresolved_gaps: These records do not quantify how much debugging difficulty across all deep learning applications was caused by opacity.
A successful factual edit does not establish comprehensive understanding or a general-purpose debugging method.
